01

Scalable AI-Enabled Curriculum and Assessment Architecture

2 Hour Learning / Alpha Schools

AI-Driven English Language Arts Learning Strategist & Curriculum DRI · 12/2025 to present

Context

A national network of 50+ campuses uses AI-powered adaptive platforms. Each learner advances at their own demonstrated level rather than by age or grade.

Challenge

Content had to be built at very high volume and still be rigorous, consistent, mapped to standards and usable by adaptive software. That could not be done one lesson at a time.

My responsibilities

  • Directly Responsible Individual for Grades 3–8 Language Arts and PreK–12 Vocabulary across the system
  • Course and program architecture, standards mapping and rigour calibration
  • Assessment design and quality control, including item-level analysis and redesign
  • Cross-functional work with learning science, engineering, product and academic leadership

Approach & solution

  • Defined a layered architecture: standards → components → subskill lessons → assessment items → mastery rules
  • Calibrated item difficulty to external benchmarks (NWEA MAP RIT bands, Bloom's taxonomy distributions)
  • Wrote reusable specifications so content and structured data could be produced consistently and consumed by softwareto verify
  • Designed AI-graded open-response assessment alongside selected-response itemsto verify

Curriculum architectureAssessment designSpecification writingAI-enabled product collaborationQuality assurance
ADocumented

What I did

I architected specification-driven courses and assessment banks that power AI-enabled, mastery-based learning across a 50+ campus network.

CProposed application

Transfer to public service workforce development

  • A public service AI curriculum built once as a modular architecture, then reused across ministries and roles
  • Scenario-based item banks that test safe, correct AI use in realistic government tasks
  • Specifications that let the Ministry, DICT or an external vendor build learning content to one quality standard

This experience comes from K–12 education. It shows I can design and scale learning systems. It is not evidence of public service workforce outcomes.

02

Analytics-Driven Learning Performance and Intervention Systems

2 Hour Learning / Alpha Schools

AI-Driven English Language Arts Learning Strategist & Curriculum DRI

Context

Adaptive learning produces rich data on each learner: assessment scores, accuracy, experience points and time-on-task. It is only useful if someone turns it into action.

Challenge

Some learners were on the wrong level, some assessments were mis-calibrated, and some students had no active course assignment. All of these were hidden in system-wide data.

My responsibilities

  • Individual placement and performance reviews using MAP RIT scores, XP, accuracy and time-on-task data
  • Querying student data across all campuses to identify and resolve enrolment gaps
  • Item-level analysis to surface mis-calibrated, low-rigour or decontextualised questions
  • Translating data insights into classroom interventions with campus leads and guides

Approach & solution

  • Combined several indicators to decide whether each learner was correctly placed, at risk or ready to advance
  • Ran system-wide queries so every eligible learner had an active Language and Vocabulary assignment
  • Redesigned weak tests with passage-based items and balanced answer keys
  • Built analytics dashboards that track learning performance and progressionto verify
AVerified scale & evidence
Grades 3–8Language placement reviews across the system
All campusesqueried for enrolment gaps
Dashboardsto verifytracking performance & progression

Relevant competencies

Learning analyticsData-informed decision-makingAssessment validityIntervention designStakeholder coordination
ADocumented

What I did

I used learning data to find mis-placed and at-risk learners, close enrolment gaps and drive targeted interventions across campuses.

CProposed application

Transfer to public service workforce development

  • An adoption and capability dashboard showing participation, competency and confidence by department
  • Early identification of teams that need coaching or follow-up support
  • Assessment quality review, so pilot results reflect real capability and not test artefacts

03

Multi-Campus Institutional Learning and Professional Development

KnowledgeLink · Barstow Schools in China · St. Mary's Online Academy

Chief Academic Officer · Regional Dean · Principal & Academic Dean · Dean of Faculty · 2019–2025

Context

KnowledgeLink operates American international schools and an online U.S. high school diploma program for international students. They work across campuses, regulators and accreditation bodies.

Challenge

Teaching quality, policies and standards had to be consistent across several campuses and an online program. Each site was growing and had its own staff, culture and regulatory needs.

My responsibilities

  • Directed academic operations for a multi-campus network of American international schools (Chief Academic Officer)
  • Directed academic and operational management across four campuses serving over 1,200 students (Regional Dean)
  • Standardised academic policies, handbooks and course catalogues; led curriculum alignment and audits
  • Designed onboarding, in-service training, coaching and performance evaluation for faculty

Approach & solution

  • Cross-campus quality assurance and continuous-improvement initiatives
  • Data-driven discussions to guide academic policy decisions
  • Blended learning models for the online diploma program
  • Mentoring of academic leaders, plus faculty recruitment and development

CProposed application

Transfer to public service workforce development

  • Consistent AI training standards and quality assurance across ministries, departments and agencies
  • Training-of-trainers and departmental AI champion networks
  • Policy-aligned onboarding so new public officers learn approved AI practice from day one

These results are institutional leadership responsibilities in education. They are not government engagements.

04

Applied Workforce Research and Evaluation

Virtuous Sea Corporation

Chief Research Officer (fractional / consulting) · 04/2025 to present

Context

An international education and workforce intelligence organization needed rigorous research to inform the decisions of institutions, employers and policymakers.

Challenge

Turning mixed qualitative and quantitative evidence into findings that are credible, ethical and useful to decision-makers.

My responsibilities

  • Lead applied research strategy and a multi-year research agenda, including workforce readiness and career outcomes
  • Direct survey design, interview protocols, mixed-methods studies and data analysis
  • Supervise research staff and collaborators for methodological rigour, data integrity and ethical compliance
  • Author and oversee reports, white papers and presentations for institutions, employers and policymakers

Approach & solution

  • Mixed-methods designs that pair survey data with interviews
  • Ethics and data-integrity controls built into each study
  • Plain-language translation of findings into actionable recommendations
  • Proprietary research frameworks for workforce intelligence
